applicantTitle: TEST: J27 Electrical communication across fungal networks
layAbstract: Fungi grow into branching networks. We want to learn whether electrical changes let one branch tell another when food is nearby. We will watch electrical signals while introducing food to one part of a network. The work could show how an organism without nerves coordinates its growth.
summaryFields:
Scientific Question: Do electrical signals coordinate distant fungal branches?
Potential Impact: Explain coordination without a nervous system. Establish how local nutrient signals affect network growth.
Risks: Signals may decay across branch junctions.
Enabling Advances: The team has demonstrated a fluorescent voltage sensor in fungal cells.
New Area: Electrical signaling between fungal branches.
Peer Groups: Fungal growth and signaling labs.
Prior Support: No award addresses electrical transmission between fungal branches.
proposalText:
[page 1]
Project Narrative
Fungal networks redistribute resources after a branch encounters nutrients. The project asks whether electrical signals coordinate distant branches. The team will deliver nutrients locally and measure electrical signals before and after the stimulus.
[page 2]
Preliminary Data and Approach
The team has demonstrated a fluorescent voltage sensor in fungal cells. Live microscopy will follow signal propagation across junctions. Signals may decay across branch junctions, leaving transmission unresolved.
